meta.title: Dix.Tax: tax forms for your property abroad
meta.description: Own a home in another country? Dix.Tax prepares the numbers for the forms that come with it: the Swiss tax return, Spain's Modelo 210 and Germany's Anlage V.

founder.title: Why I built this
body: I am Aleksej Dix. I file my taxes in Switzerland and own several apartments abroad. The first time they had to go into my tax return, I paid for the answers myself: advisers, evenings with German directives, and a lot of second guessing.

The rules turned out to be simple once somebody explains them. Many people in Switzerland own a home in another country and face the same form, often in a language that is not their own. Dix.Tax puts what I learned into ten minutes.

footer.disclaimer: Dix.Tax is an information and calculation tool. It is not tax or legal advice and does not replace an adviser. Rules and practice can change; check your figures before you file.
footer.sources: Based on the Zurich tax return guide (Wegleitung) and the cantonal valuation directive.
footer.tagline: Tax forms for people who own property abroad.

hub.title: Property abroad comes with a tax form. We prepare it.
hub.lead: A home in another country means a filing where you live, where the home stands, or both. Dix.Tax asks a few plain questions and gives you the exact number for every line, explained in your language.
hub.bothBody: A flat in Valencia owned from Zurich needs Modelo 210 in Spain and a line in the Zurich tax return. The two use different values and different rules. Dix.Tax keeps them apart and gets both right.

chZurich.name: Swiss tax return
chZurich.who: You live in Switzerland and own property in another country.
chZurich.what: Tax value, notional rent and the flat deduction for the Liegenschaftenverzeichnis, plus a German note for the tax office.

modelo210.name: Modelo 210
modelo210.who: You own a home in Spain and live somewhere else.
modelo210.what: Spain's tax for owners who are not resident there. Due every year, even if the home is never rented.

anlageV.name: Anlage V
anlageV.who: You rent out property in Germany and live somewhere else.
anlageV.what: The rental schedule of the German tax return, with depreciation and deductible costs.

trust.title: Why you can rely on the numbers

items.title: Every rule has a source
items.body: Each percentage and form line comes from an official guide, law or directive, and we name it next to the number.

items.title: Calculations are tested
items.body: Reference cases with known results run automatically on every change, so a fix in one place cannot quietly break another.

items.title: Your data stays with you
items.body: Everything is calculated in your browser. Nothing you type into a calculator is sent to us.

items.title: A person stands behind it
items.body: Dix.Tax is built by Aleksej Dix in Zurich, who files these forms for his own properties.
